annotations.text:
The same problem, transposed

Salary had nineteen empty rows. Compare has three empty columns: of forty matrix cells, twenty-seven are "—", because only one of the four companies has a figure at SDE1 in Madrid.

The top says "Locked" five times — three metric tiles and four decision tiles, all needing two supported values that do not exist.

And the one human explanation on the page, "Decision rationale", is collapsed behind a disclosure. That is the summary, and it is hidden.

The salary treatment, applied

Same green band, same one-line control bar, same card table — so the two pages read as one product.

The band carries one thing salary's does not: a comparison of one is not a comparison. It names the three companies with nothing, and offers the three that would fix it.

In the matrix, an empty column states its reason once in the header instead of repeating a different phrasing of "no data" in every cell — "No matching observation", "No supported recurring-cash value", "Needs a validated net-cash estimate" — and goes quiet below.

The collapsed rationale is gone: the band is the rationale.
